title: How to connect zoom to google calendar on mac: desktop and web steps for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to connect Zoom to Google Calendar on Mac: steps
description: Learn how to connect Zoom to Google Calendar on Mac. Use the desktop app for Zoom Calendar, the web portal for two-way sync, and fix common errors.
targetKeyword: how to connect zoom to google calendar on mac
intro: Open the Zoom desktop app on your Mac, sign in, go to the Meetings tab, and click Sign in with Google to connect Zoom Calendar. For meetings that sync both ways, also connect Google Calendar in the Zoom web portal at Profile > Others > Configure Calendar and Contacts Service.
tldr: Zoom Calendar: sign in on the Mac desktop app, then use Meetings > Sign in with Google.
Two-way sync: connect Google Calendar in the Zoom web portal at Profile > Others, then sign out and back in on the desktop app.
Update first. Zoom's update policy lists 6.0.2 as the macOS minimum.
Connect one calendar service at a time, and sign in with only the Google account you want to sync.
If sync stops, reauthorize Google Calendar from your Zoom profile page, then send a test invite.

blocks.text: There are two ways to connect Zoom to Google Calendar on a Mac, and they do different jobs. Zoom Calendar is set up in the Zoom desktop app, and it shows your Google events inside Zoom. Calendar and Contact Integration is set up in the Zoom web portal, and it syncs your meetings in both directions. Pick the desktop path if you want to see your calendar in Zoom. Pick the web path if you want Zoom meetings to appear in Google Calendar. Many people use both, so this guide covers both, starting with the desktop app.
Before you start: version, accounts and calendar

Start with the version. Zoom's update policy lists 6.0.2 as the minimum macOS version. Zoom's calendar article still says 5.14.5, which looks out of date. Treat 6.0.2 as your floor, and update before you begin. A build below the minimum causes more trouble than any single setting, so this step saves time later.

Next, check your accounts. You need a Zoom account you can sign in to directly. You also need a Google account that owns the calendar you want. Zoom Calendar supports three services: Zoom, Google, and Microsoft 365 (Exchange). This guide covers Google only, so skip the Microsoft steps.

items: A Zoom account you can sign in to directly, not only through single sign-on (SSO).
Zoom desktop app 6.0.2 or later on your Mac.
A Google account that owns the calendar you want to sync.
A browser for the Google sign-in and for the Zoom web portal.
Admin approval if your company manages Zoom calendar integration.

blocks.text: Connect Zoom Calendar from the Mac desktop app

Open the Zoom desktop app and sign in. The sign-in screen offers Sign in, Join a meeting, and Sign up. Choose Sign in, because calendar setup needs a signed-in account. After you sign in, Zoom's calendar article tells you to click the Meetings tab. Zoom's getting-started article describes a Calendar tab in the left sidebar and does not mention a Meetings tab. Labels can differ between builds. Look for the tab that holds the calendar options, and use that one.

Click Sign in with Google. Zoom opens Profile permissions in your browser, so keep that browser tab open. On the permissions page, set Calendar to Read and Write. Email access is optional, so you can leave it off for calendar sync. Then select Google, click Next, sign in to your Google account, and click Allow. Read and Write matters most. If a meeting never reaches Google, check this permission first.

Choose the Google account carefully. The account you sign in with receives the sync, so it decides which calendar gets the events. If you use a personal Gmail account for Zoom and a work account for meetings, connect the account that holds your work calendar. Connecting the wrong account is the most common reason people think sync is broken when it is only pointed at the wrong place.
Set up two-way sync in the Zoom web portal

Calendar and Contact Integration lives in the web portal, not in the desktop app. Sign in to the Zoom web portal in your browser with the same Zoom account. Open your profile. Then go to Profile > Others > Configure Calendar and Contacts Service. Select Google, check the permissions for Read, Write, and Shared, and click Next. Sign in to Google and click Allow.

Zoom creates a Google Connector app connection in the Zoom Marketplace during this step. You do not need to create that connection yourself. After setup, sign out of the Zoom desktop app and sign back in. Zoom says two-way syncing is on by default, so you do not need to find a separate switch.

Two-way sync means meetings you create in Zoom can appear in Google Calendar, and changes can move in both directions. Zoom also warns about one habit. Changing a meeting's time in the desktop app creates a separate Google event. It does not update the original. Plan reschedules with that in mind, and check Google Calendar after you move a meeting.

blocks.text: Zoom allows one third-party calendar service per user for calendar and contact syncing. That rule matters when you already use another service. Remove the current one before you add a new one. Admins can force a specific service and restrict the permissions users grant.

A simple rule helps here. If you only want to see your Google events inside Zoom, start with the desktop path. If you want meetings to land in Google Calendar, do both. The desktop sign-in gives Zoom access, and the web portal handles the two-way sync.
Worked example: one Mac, two Google accounts

Say you have a work Google account and a personal one. Both are signed in to your browser on your Mac. You want Zoom to sync with the work calendar. Zoom's troubleshooting lists several Google accounts signed in at once as a common cause of sync failure. Sign out of the personal account in the browser first, or use a browser profile where only the work account is signed in.

Next, connect Zoom to the work account. Then press ⌘D to schedule a test meeting, and invite a second address you can check. Look for the event in the work calendar, then in the personal one. If it lands in the right calendar, you are done. If it lands in the wrong one, sign out of the wrong account in the browser and reconnect.
Keyboard shortcuts and where Settings lives

Once Calendar is connected, a few shortcuts save clicks. ⌘D schedules a meeting. ⌘J joins one. ⌘E opens global search, which helps when you cannot remember which meeting you need. ⇧⌘J shows or hides the Calendar side panel. ⇧⌘I copies the invite link, which helps when you paste a meeting into a Google event by hand.

To review or change shortcuts, click your profile picture, click Settings, then click Keyboard shortcuts. Zoom's docs do not list a ⌘, shortcut for Settings, so use the profile picture route. Zoom's shortcut article lists Settings only through that menu.
Test the connection before you rely on it

Run one test before your next real meeting. Press ⌘D, pick a time in the next hour, and invite a second address you control. Then check that address and Google Calendar in a browser. A working setup shows the event with the meeting link. If the event does not appear, work through the fixes below.
Repeat the test after any change to your Google account, your browser, or your Zoom version. A test takes about two minutes. It catches a broken link before a client or a manager finds it for you.
Fix sync when Google Calendar stops updating

Most sync failures have one of five causes. Zoom's troubleshooting names incorrect setup, expired authorization, missing permissions, several Google accounts signed in at once, and SSO-only sign-in. Ask which of these changed. If sync worked last week and stopped, start with authorization. If it never worked, start with accounts and permissions.

When authorization expires, events stop syncing until you reconnect. Open your Zoom profile page in the web portal and reauthorize Google Calendar. Then send a test invite. Do not assume the fix worked until the event shows up in Google Calendar.

The Zoom articles contain no Mac-only error messages. The fixes apply to Mac and Windows alike. If your Mac shows a specific error, search Zoom's support site for the exact wording first, then compare it with the causes above.
Mistakes people make when connecting Zoom to Google Calendar

items: Signing in with a second Google account in the same browser, then wondering which calendar Zoom used.
Skipping the Read and Write setting because it looked optional.
Changing a meeting time in the desktop app and expecting Google to update the same event. Zoom creates a separate event instead.
Keeping an old calendar service connected, then trying to add a second one.
Updating Zoom only after sync fails, instead of before setup.

blocks.text: Before you ask your admin for help

Some company accounts block calendar setup. Before you email your admin, gather four facts. Note your Zoom version, the Google account you tried, the exact error text, and the step where it failed. Those four details let your admin answer in one reply instead of three.

Ask two direct questions. Is calendar and contact integration enabled for my account? Which calendar service am I allowed to use? Zoom says admins can enable the integration, force a service, and restrict permissions, so those questions match how the system works.
Versions, minimums and why the numbers change

Zoom updates its platform minimums on a schedule. Its policy page says Zoom sets a minimum version every 3 months. The same page lists 7.2.5 as the macOS fast-track version as of 10/31/26. It lists 7.1.9 as the slow-track and prompted version as of 9/27/26. The minimum it lists for macOS is 6.0.2.

The calendar articles do not show a last-updated date. Treat the version numbers as a snapshot. Check the live policy page before you rely on a specific build. Update the app when Zoom asks, and do not skip a prompt just because sync works today.
Privacy and permissions: what you allow Zoom to access

The Google sign-in gives Zoom calendar access. Read and Write lets Zoom read your events and write to the calendar. Email access is optional, and you can skip it for sync. Only sign in with the Google account whose calendar you want Zoom to use.

If you are unsure, ask your admin before you click Allow. Admins can restrict services and permissions, and they can require one service for everyone. A blocked setup can mean your admin chose a different policy, not that your Mac has a fault.
What to do after the connection works

Once sync works, create meetings in Zoom and check Google Calendar. For new meetings, read the [schedule a meeting in Zoom](/how-to/schedule-a-meeting-in-zoom) guide. For meetings that already exist, read the [join a meeting in Zoom](/how-to/join-a-meeting-in-zoom) guide. Both guides are the next step once your calendar shows the right events.
Keep a note of the Google account you connected. Reconnecting after an expired authorization goes faster when you know which account it was.

faq.question: Can I connect Zoom to Google Calendar on a Mac without the desktop app?
faq.answer: Only partly. Zoom says the first Zoom Calendar setup can only be done in the desktop app, not the mobile app. Calendar and Contact Integration uses the web portal, but you still sign out and back in on the desktop app to finish.

faq.question: Which Zoom version do I need for Google Calendar on a Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom's update policy lists 6.0.2 as the minimum for macOS. Zoom's calendar article says 5.14.5, which looks out of date. Treat 6.0.2 as the floor and update the app before you start the setup.

faq.question: Can Zoom Calendar use Google and Microsoft 365 at the same time?
faq.answer: No. Each user can connect only one third-party calendar service for calendar and contact syncing at a time. Pick one service, and remove it before you switch to another.

faq.question: Why did changing a meeting time create two events in Google Calendar?
faq.answer: Zoom says that changing a meeting time in the desktop app creates a separate Google event instead of updating the original. Delete the extra event in Google Calendar, then check that the original shows the right time.

faq.question: Is two-way sync on by default?
faq.answer: Yes. Zoom says bi-directional syncing is enabled by default after you finish the web portal setup. Sign out of the desktop app and sign back in to start it.

faq.question: Why does Zoom stop syncing with Google Calendar after some time?
faq.answer: Zoom says events stop syncing when the Google authorization is disconnected or expires. Reauthorize Google Calendar from your Zoom profile page, then send a test invite to confirm the sync works again.

faq.question: Do I need admin approval to connect Google Calendar?
faq.answer: It depends on your account. Zoom says admins must enable calendar and contact integration, and they can force a service and restrict permissions. If setup is blocked, ask your admin which service they allow.

faq.question: Which Mac shortcuts help once Google Calendar is connected?
faq.answer: Zoom lists ⌘D to schedule a meeting, ⌘J to join one, ⌘E for global search, and ⇧⌘J for the Calendar side panel. Shortcut settings sit under your profile picture, then Settings, then Keyboard shortcuts.

steps.name: Update Zoom to 6.0.2 or later
steps.text: Check your Zoom version before you start. Zoom's update policy lists 6.0.2 as the macOS minimum. Zoom's calendar article says 5.14.5, which looks out of date, so treat 6.0.2 as the real floor. If your build is older, update it first, then continue.
steps.tip: Zoom says it sets a new minimum version about every 3 months. Repeat this check if sync breaks later.

steps.name: Sign in to the Zoom desktop app
steps.text: Open Zoom on your Mac and click Sign in on the sign-in screen. The screen also offers Join a meeting and Sign up, but this setup needs Sign in. Enter your Zoom account details.
steps.tip: If your account only works through single sign-on (SSO), calendar setup may be blocked. Ask your admin.

steps.name: Open the Meetings tab
steps.text: After you sign in, click the Meetings tab. Zoom's calendar article uses this label. If your build shows Calendar in the left sidebar instead, click that tab and keep going.
steps.tip: Labels can differ between builds. Look for the tab that holds the calendar options.

steps.name: Click Sign in with Google
steps.text: Click Sign in with Google. Zoom opens Profile permissions in your browser. Keep that browser tab open until you finish the next steps.

steps.name: Set Calendar to Read and Write
steps.text: On the Profile permissions page, set Calendar to Read and Write. Email access is optional, so you can leave it off. Read and Write is the setting that lets Zoom write to your calendar.
steps.tip: If a meeting never reaches Google, check this setting before anything else.

steps.name: Select Google and click Next
steps.text: Select Google as your calendar service. Zoom Calendar also supports Zoom and Microsoft 365 (Exchange), but this guide uses Google. Click Next.

steps.name: Sign in to Google and click Allow
steps.text: Sign in with the Google account whose calendar you want to use. Click Allow to finish the Zoom Calendar setup.
steps.tip: If several Google accounts are signed in at once, sign out of the extra ones first. Several accounts can cause sync to fail.

steps.name: Open your profile in the web portal
steps.text: In your browser, sign in to the Zoom web portal with the same Zoom account. Open your profile. The two-way sync setup lives here, not in the desktop app.

steps.name: Open Configure Calendar and Contacts Service
steps.text: Click Others, then click Configure Calendar and Contacts Service. Select Google. Check the permissions for Read, Write, and Shared, then click Next.

steps.name: Sign in to Google and allow the connector
steps.text: Sign in to Google, then click Allow. Zoom creates a Google Connector app connection in the Zoom Marketplace as part of this step.

steps.name: Sign out and back in on the desktop app
steps.text: Return to the Zoom desktop app. Sign out, then sign back in. Two-way sync is on by default after setup, so you do not need to switch anything else on.

steps.name: Send a test invite
steps.text: Press ⌘D to schedule a meeting. Pick a time in the next hour, invite a second address you control, and send it. Then open Google Calendar in a browser and find the event.
steps.tip: If the event does not appear, check which Google account you signed in with, then work through the fixes below.

shortcuts.action: Show or hide the Calendar side panel

troubleshooting.problem: Events stop syncing between Zoom and Google Calendar
troubleshooting.fix: Your Google authorization probably expired or disconnected. Open your Zoom profile page in the web portal and reauthorize Google Calendar. Send a test invite to confirm the events sync again.

troubleshooting.problem: Sync fails and several Google accounts are signed in
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the In use integration. Sign out of all Google accounts in the browser, then sign in with the target account only. Reconnect, then send a test invite.
Reconnect and set Calendar to Read and Write. Missing permissions are one of the causes Zoom lists for calendar problems.

troubleshooting.problem: Your account only signs in with single sign-on
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom lists SSO-only sign-in as a cause of calendar problems. Ask your Zoom admin whether calendar integration is enabled for your account and which service they allow.

troubleshooting.problem: A meeting time change creates a second Google event
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom creates a separate Google event when you change a meeting time in the desktop app. Delete the duplicate in Google Calendar, and check that the original event is correct.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot add a second calendar service
troubleshooting.fix: Each user can connect one third-party calendar service at a time. Remove the current one, then connect the new one. Admins can also limit which services are offered.
